literal: State having feared, among those who renounced all, killing having feared, non-killing he who considers is foremost.
translation: Among all those who have renounced the world out of fear for its fleeting state, the foremost is he who fears taking life and commits to non-killing.
modern: வாழ்க்கையின் நிலையாமையைக் கண்டு அஞ்சிப் பற்றுகளை விட்டவர்கள் அனைவரிலும், ஓர் உயிரைக் கொலை செய்வதற்கு அஞ்சி அதைக் கொல்லாமல் இருப்பதைப் பற்றிச் சிந்திப்பவனே தலைசிறந்தவன்.
explanation: This couplet evaluates the greatness of those who have renounced worldly life. While many become ascetics because they fear the unstable and painful state of earthly existence, this alone does not make them the greatest. The text declares that among all renunciants, the absolute foremost is the one who fears taking life and actively upholds the principle of non-killing. The word 'talai' literally means head, but here it signifies the chief or highest position among all virtuous people.
